encryption.title: Encryption & Privacy
encryption.description: Organization data (trackers and documents) is encrypted in transit and at rest and isolated per organization. Depending on your organization's setup, encryption keys are either held only by members' devices, or managed by Nimbalyst so the organization is reachable from the web, CLI, and cloud agents.

pricing.realtimeExample: Example: 10 minutes with each side speaking 5 is roughly $0.50, before coding-agent costs.

cloudflareSandboxNode.title: Agent node
cloudflareSandboxNode.description: Connecting installs a Nimbalyst agent in the sandbox and signs it in as one of your devices. Your Claude Code subscription login is copied into the sandbox so the agent can use it. The sandbox discards everything inside it whenever it sleeps, so anything the agent has not pushed to git is lost and the node has to be connected again.
cloudflareSandboxNode.noWorkspace: Open a workspace first. The node clones that workspace's repository and branch.
cloudflareSandboxNode.disconnectConfirm: Disconnecting asks the agent to stop, ending any session it is running, and revokes its sync credential so reconnecting issues a new one. Anything it wrote and has not pushed stays in the sandbox until the sandbox next sleeps, and is then lost.

fidelity.structured: Reports every file it changes directly, including the file's contents before the edit. Diff review and the Files Edited list are exact.

fidelity.none: Does not report the files it changes. Nimbalyst infers them by watching the project folder, so diff review is approximate.

database.title: Database Storage
database.description: Local storage engine for sessions, trackers, and document history. New installs start on SQLite. Installs that already have a PGLite database stay on it: automatic migration is turned off while the migration is being reworked, so nothing moves unless you start it from this panel.

dryRun.title: Test the SQLite migration (dry run)
dryRun.description: Copies your data into a throwaway SQLite database alongside the live one, reports row counts and integrity, then keeps the successful copy for switching. Your real PGLite database is never touched. Available only while PGLite is active.

adoptConfirm.title: Switch to SQLite
adoptConfirm.message:
Switch to the dry-run SQLite copy?

Nimbalyst will:
  1. Close the current PGLite database
  2. Copy anything new since the dry-run ({{age}} ago)
  3. Make SQLite the active backend
  4. Preserve the old PGLite for rollback

A relaunch is required after switching.

rollbackConfirm.title: Restore PGLite database
rollbackConfirm.message: Restore the preserved PGLite database? You will lose any data created since the migration. Requires a relaunch.

migrate.title: Migrate to SQLite
migrate.description: Moves all your data from PGLite to SQLite. The original PGLite directory is preserved at {{dir}} and can be restored from this panel.

migrated.title: Migrated to SQLite
migrated.description: Your data is already stored in the faster SQLite backend. No further migration is needed.

restore.title: Restore previous PGLite database
restore.description: Puts the most recent preserved PGLite copy back in front of the app. Data created since the migration will not be in it. The copies themselves are listed below.

modal.description: This runs in one uninterrupted flow and preserves the original PGLite directory for rollback.
modal.cutoverDetail: Preserving the previous PGLite directory and flipping the active backend.

recovery.title: Databases set aside on this computer
recovery.description: Earlier versions of Nimbalyst moved a database aside when opening it failed. These copies are kept indefinitely and are never removed automatically. A copy being here does not mean the database you are using now is damaged.

reasons.candidateMissing: This copy is no longer on disk.
reasons.alreadyResolved: You have already dealt with this copy.
reasons.candidateInvalid: This copy is not a database Nimbalyst can read.
reasons.candidateNotMateriallyRicher: This copy does not appear to hold anything the current database is missing.
reasons.candidateUnreadable: Nimbalyst could not read this copy well enough to describe it.
reasons.liveUnreadable: Nimbalyst could not read the current database, so it cannot compare the two.
reasons.factsChangedWhileReading: The files changed while Nimbalyst was reading them, so it stopped rather than compare a moving target.
reasons.bothDatabasesHaveContent: This copy and the current database both hold data. Nimbalyst cannot tell which one you want.
reasons.liveEmptyButInstallLooksNew: The current database is empty, and this computer has no project history to compare it against.
reasons.liveEmptyOnEstablishedInstall: The current database is empty, but this computer has settings for projects you have used, and this copy holds data.
reasons.unknown: Nimbalyst has no description for this result.

offer.title: One of these copies may hold data your current database does not
offer.reviewBelow: {{reason}} Review it below before deciding anything.

result.restored: Restored from {{name}}. The database that was live before this, and the copy it was restored from, are both still on disk. Relaunch Nimbalyst to use the restored database.
result.rolledBack: The database you were using has been put back, and every copy is still on disk.
result.notChanged: The database you were using was not changed, and every copy is still on disk.

candidate.cannotRestore: This build cannot restore a PGLite copy onto a SQLite database. You can still open the copy in Finder and keep it.

confirm.title: Restore from a set-aside database
confirm.description: Read what each copy becomes. Nimbalyst does not delete any of them, now or later.
confirm.keptCopy: The copy above, unchanged. Restoring reads it; it is never modified.
confirm.keptSnapshot: A snapshot of the database you are using now, taken and verified before anything moves, saved beside it with pre-restore and a timestamp in its name.
confirm.keptDisplaced: The database you are using now, moved aside with displaced and a timestamp in its name.
confirm.verificationNote: The copy is verified before it replaces anything. If verification or any later step fails, the database you are using now stays in place and every copy remains on disk. Nimbalyst must be relaunched afterwards either way.
confirm.acknowledge: I have read which database is replaced and which copies are kept.

blocked.title: Automatic migration is held back on this computer

reasons.backupDwarfsLive: A database set aside on this computer is much larger than the one in use, so Nimbalyst will not copy the one in use without you looking first.
reasons.projectsWithoutSessions: This computer has settings for projects you have opened, but the database Nimbalyst would copy from has no sessions in it.
reasons.sourceUnreadable: Nimbalyst could not read the database it would copy from, and an unreadable database is not treated as an empty one.
reasons.sourceMissing: The database Nimbalyst would copy from is not on disk.
reasons.insufficientDisk: There is not enough free disk space to hold both databases during the copy.
reasons.unknown: Nimbalyst recorded a reason it cannot describe in this build.

blocked.recorded: Recorded {{date}}. Nimbalyst re-checks this on its own if what it measures changes. Nothing has been copied, moved, or deleted.
blocked.clearExplanation: Clearing this lets a later launch assess the migration again. It does not start a migration and does not change any data, but it does remove the check that stopped Nimbalyst from copying a database it could not confirm was the one holding your work. Look at any set-aside copies first.
blocked.clearButton: Clear this and re-check on the next launch

copies.title: PGLite copies kept from a migration
copies.description: A migration keeps the PGLite database it copied from. These stay until you remove them; Nimbalyst does not delete them on a schedule.
copies.rollbackSource: This is the copy "Restore from preserved PGLite" would use.
copies.notRollbackSource: Kept on disk. It is not the copy a rollback would use.

deleteConfirm.title: Delete a preserved copy
deleteConfirm.permanentlyRemoves: This permanently removes {{size}} — the PGLite database as it stood on {{date}}, before it was migrated. Sessions and document history that exist only in this copy cannot be recovered afterwards.
deleteConfirm.rollbackWarning: This is the copy a rollback restores from. Once it is gone, this install cannot be put back onto PGLite.
deleteConfirm.notTouched: The database you are using now is not touched.
deleteConfirm.acknowledge: I understand this copy cannot be recovered after deleting it.

adopt.title: Switch to your dry-run SQLite copy
adopt.description: A successful dry-run from {{age}} is saved on disk ({{rows}} rows). Nimbalyst can promote it to be your active database — it'll copy anything new since the dry-run, then flip the backend flag. The current PGLite directory is preserved for rollback.
adopt.switched_zero: Switched to SQLite. Caught up {{rows}} new rows in {{duration}}. Please relaunch Nimbalyst for the change to take effect.
adopt.switched_one: Switched to SQLite. Caught up {{rows}} new row in {{duration}}. Please relaunch Nimbalyst for the change to take effect.
adopt.switched_other: Switched to SQLite. Caught up {{rows}} new rows in {{duration}}. Please relaunch Nimbalyst for the change to take effect.

migration.historyWarning_one: Migration completed with {{formattedCount}} document-history entry omitted. These entries are unavailable in history, but their original data is retained in a local recovery record. The original PGLite database is also retained. Sessions and messages were not skipped.
migration.historyWarning_other: Migration completed with {{formattedCount}} document-history entries omitted.
